Forecast Discussion

NWS Detroit/Pontiac · 1238 PM EST Fri Nov 13 2026
 

- Showers steadily shift offshore tonight and Saturday, then 
turning drier and warm next week.

&&

.AVIATION...

Mostly MVFR cigs with very light rain and melting snow downwind of 
Lake Huron across most of southeast Michigan early this afternoon. 
Weak surface ridging building into southern Lower Michigan early 
this evening is expected to support low level drying as winds shift 
a touch more out of northwest, confining lake effect activity to the 
Thumb region tonight. Thus, partial clearing and VFR ceilings are 
expected this evening into tonight at all taf sites. Prolonged low 
level northwest flow should eventually result into borderline 
MVFR/VFR stratus tomorrow morning, though exact timing remains 
uncertain. Once the low clouds return, they should remain locked in 
through the day tomorrow. 

For DTW...Light rain showers with embedded melting snow this 
afternoon will dissipate by early this evening as low levels dry out 
and partial clearing takes place. It is possible a leftover VFR 
ceiling 3000-5000 ft lingers this evening into tonight, but 
confidence is low. Low clouds will likely hold off until tomorrow 
morning (between 11 and 15z) before returning. 

.DTW THRESHOLD PROBABILITIES...

* High for ceilings at or below 5,000 feet this afternoon, low this 
  evening and tonight, high tomorrow.

* Medium for light rain/melting snow mix this afternoon.
